text: xc is a heterogeneous data-parallel language. Write an ordinary loop, in xc or in C, and xcc runs it across every CPU core, on the GPU through Metal, CUDA, Vulkan or WebGPU, across several GPUs from different vendors at once, or on a GPU on another machine, and keeps whichever is fastest. The kernels are generated by xcc itself and carried in the executable, so a build needs no GPU toolkit. Documentation, benchmarks and downloads are at https://compile-xc.org . This repository holds the compiler, its GUI framework and the tools and applications built with them. It is one repository, but it is worked on as several separate streams, and each stream stays inside its own tree. Two rules keep the streams' work apart: Pull requests, from outside contributors and from the streams alike, keep main always gated: private/ is not part of the repository. It is ignored by git and holds the working rules, the notes on open and fixed bugs, and other material that is never published. Nothing under it is ever committed. Build and install the compiler first (see compiler/USAGE.md ), then build whichever other tree you are working in against it. Settings that depend on your machines, such as the Linux test host or the location of the GEM desktop sources, live in build.env at the repository root. Copy build.env.template to build.env and fill in the values you need. build.env is ignored by git. A variable left empty turns off the step that needs it. Pull requests are welcome. CONTRIBUTING.md says how a change gets into main : the contributor licence agreement you sign once, where changes go, and how to build and test with an installed release. Everyone taking part agrees to the code of conduct . Security problems are reported privately, as SECURITY.md describes. Every benchmark figure on the site is measured on hardware the project has bought, and the machines that matter most for data-parallel work are expensive. A loan or donation goes straight into the compiler: a back end and a runtime tuned on the device, kept working by being tested on it every release, and its figures published beside the others. We would most like: If you make or sell hardware like this and would like xc to run well on it, write to xc@oobergeek.net . See LICENSING.md . My apologies but I wasn't great at keeping private details out of the ~3000 or so checkins made to get this far, and the thought of going back and changing everything didn't really appeal. So, clean start, and I'll be more diligent from now on...
